status.en: 236 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Plateau State.
status.nb: 236 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Plateau State.

summary.en: Recent attacks include gunmen killing 15 soldiers in a convoy in Borno and a bomb explosion on a Borno road that killed nine soldiers, while bandits killed three policemen in Zamfara. In Benue, police rescued an abducted Catholic priest and seven others, and in Plateau gunmen attacked herders, killing two and injuring six, with reports of house burnings targeting Fulani communities. Islamist jihadists burned an evangelist alive in Adamawa and kidnapped a Catholic priest in Benue, also striking bases. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Nylige angrep inkluderer væpnede menn som drepte 15 soldater i en konvoi i Borno, og en bombeeksplosjon på en vei i Borno som drepte ni soldater, mens banditter drepte tre politifolk i Zamfara. I Benue reddet politiet en bortført katolsk prest og syv andre, og i Plateau angrep væpnede menn hyrdefolk, drepte to og såret seks, med rapporter om brente hus som rammet Fulani-samfunn. Islamistiske jihadister brente en evangelisk predikant levende i Adamawa og kidnappet en katolsk prest i Benue, og rammet også baser. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
